Wyszogrod New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Wyszogród, Poland

Not demolished. Established around 1831 to relieve overcrowding at Wyszogród's old cemetery - and prompted by a cholera epidemic - this newer cemetery served a community that reached 2,465 residents by 1921, most deported via Czerwińsk and Nowy Dwór Mazowiecki to Auschwitz-Birkenau in 1941-1942. Germans tore out matzevot during the war to build street curbs, some taken as far as Bodzanów. Poland's District Jewish Committee unveiled a commemorative monument in 1947, and in 1989, Wyszogród expatriates in the United States funded an obelisk honoring the local Jewish community; cleanup continued through 1997 with support from US-based donor Marion Brzozowski.
